blocks.title: Alkenes
blocks.text: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons: compounds of hydrogen and carbon only whose molecules contain carbon-to-carbon double bonds (alkynes contain triple bonds). Alkenes have two hydrogen atoms fewer than the corresponding saturated hydrocarbons, general formula CnH2n.
The following topics give the IUPAC naming of alkenes (11.6.1), their preparation by elimination reactions (11.6.2) and their physical properties.

blocks.prompt: Why does an alkene have two fewer hydrogens than the alkane with the same number of carbons?
blocks.explanation: Forming the carbon-carbon double bond uses one bonding position on each of the two carbons that in the alkane were occupied by hydrogen atoms, so CnH2n+2 becomes CnH2n: ethane C2H6 and ethene C2H4.

items: Alkenes: unsaturated hydrocarbons with C=C, CnH2n, two H fewer than the alkane.
